Situation1: A serious situation has come up in the family, and the grandparent's presence is needed.
Expectation2: Assemble and construct wooden frameworks, furniture, or cabinetry
Situation2: The carpenter is building custom cabinetry and needs to collaborate with other construction professionals to complete the project on time
Story: I stood in my workshop, the scent of sawdust thick in the air, my hands rough from hours of sanding the custom cabinetry. The blueprints were spread out before me, and I could hear the muffled voices of the electricians and plumbers waiting for my part to be finished so they could continue their work. The deadline loomed, and I knew any delay on my end would throw the whole project off schedule. My phone buzzed on the workbench. It was my daughter, her voice trembling as she explained the family emergency—my grandson needed me, right now. My heart twisted. As a grandparent, I was expected to be there, to comfort and support, to put family first. But as a carpenter, I was relied upon by my team, my absence risking not just my reputation but the livelihoods of others. I stared at the unfinished cabinet, the tools in my hands suddenly heavy, torn between the pull of family and the demands of my craft, feeling the weight of both worlds pressing in on me.
